description: Machine-checked routes from every tracked research report and GUI prototype to the governed specifications and decisions that consume it. reviewed_digest covers both sources and consumers so modifying either side requires an explicit cross-review.

routes.review_note: The research inventory and human traceability synthesis register all six owner-approved identity decisions, REV-C03-Q1 through Q6, REV-C04 standalone/offline and optional-Git integration, REV-C05 impact/reproducibility, and REV-C06 Q1/Q2 amended approvals. Q1 makes Navigator revision structure permanently visible; Q2 keeps one cohesive Release pane with persistent summaries and refuses collapse for unresolved facts. V9-A separates mutable Publish Sets from controlled issued records; V10-C establishes typed standing facts. Git and air-gap exchanges remain mapped, verified, quarantined adapter inputs. The split V1-V12 studies, distributed-collaboration re-entry, and unimplemented Global Preferences follow-ons remain linked; source-strength gates are preserved and no implementation is authorized.
The historical focus/tab incident is retained against the native terminal interaction contract.
Material rendering and regression research constrain the Rendering Book and visual proof harness.
Feedback proximity and Console research are reconciled with their guidance, shell specification, and ratified Console decision.
Compound semantics and visual language jointly constrain the universal selection contract.
Context-menu research feeds the content inventory and shell interaction specification.
The complete standards corpus is reviewed as one cross-domain input set against the standards specification and integration guidance.

The REV-C03 authority model, identity packet, split V1-V10 identity/authority studies, all six identity dispositions, Q2 successor choreography, REV-C04 offline/Git integration, REV-C05 impact/reproducibility contract, REV-C06 brief, and the split UX-V1-V12 visual study were cross-reviewed against every Publish/workspace consumer. REV-C06 Q1 adopts owner-rendered Q1-A-amended: permanent expanded Revision groups and informative empty states expose authority from Project creation; reveal-on-first-record and collapse-by-default are rejected, while future hiding/collapse is reserved to Global Preferences presentation policy. REV-C06 Q2 owner-approves Q2-A-amended: one cohesive Release pane retains all nine ReleaseCandidate section headings and typed summaries; only user-requested clean detail folds, while blockers, Unknown, stale or invalidated facts, missing requirements, and unresolved departures refuse collapse. Baseline comparison retains exactly five typed results with administrative rename under Modified; the Publish G4 seam distinguishes successor impact from derived-evidence staleness while preserving historical evidence. V8-A/Q4 preserve per-CI revision ownership and coordinated affected-revision issuance; V9-A separates editable Publish Sets from controlled issued records; V10-C makes standing typed/profile-governed. REV-C04 keeps Git optional/non-authoritative. REV-C05 requires witness-backed impact, explicit pinned-library uptake, identity-aligned comparison, immutable regeneration, and byte-identical reproduction. Full multi-writer collaboration remains reserved to dat-distributed-collaboration-architecture-lt1. V2-P, Project-owned policy, ConfigurationRef, licensed-text/source-strength gates, and planning-only status remain preserved.
Parametric editor and DXF research feed the library-authoring and footprint-system contracts.
Typography, clearance, text-engine, and manufacturing compaction research are jointly governed by the Rendering Book.
The product-mechanics research is retained against the controlling product doctrine.
Terminal state inventory and redesign research feed the native terminal contract and implementation plan.

Editor-shell and pane prototypes constrain the completed DOC-C04 Publish study alongside the shell, conformance, document/view, and pane-tiling authorities; the study extends rather than redesigns them.
The owner-disposed Console visual study remains paired with its decision and shell contract.
Context-menu visual authority and comparative open-fork evidence stay attached to the shell interaction contract.

The owner-approved DOC-C04 Publish Space visual contract is registered as one cross-linked three-file study: publish-space-study.html owns frames A-B and the complete OR-1..OR-8 index, publish-composition-study.html owns frames C-E, and publish-lifecycle-study.html owns frames F-H. The split preserves every frame anchor and ratified visual while restoring source-health; all cross-file index links resolve to the file owning their target. The contract remains integrated into specs/PUBLISH_SPACE_SPEC.md, including navigation, composition, Viewport state, revision-boundary presentation, and both type-first Pane titles. REV-C03-Q5 further clarifies that a Publish Set owns editable ordering and explicit source bindings only; separate ControlledDocuments, DocumentIssues, ReleasePackages, and Transmittals retain governed identity. Referenced-source deletion still refuses until dependencies are removed or retargeted.
The owner-reviewed selection visual study remains paired with functional and rendering authorities.
The terminal visual study remains attached to the native terminal product contract.
